inputs.name: ticks

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The environment is registered as 'cartpole' with max_episode_steps=500, order_enforce=False and disable_env_checker=True
The environment step period STEP_DT and the controller update period CONTROL_DT are both 0.02 s
The failure thresholds are 2.4 for the cart position and 12 degrees for the pole angle
The sampling ranges of cart position, pole angle, cart velocity and pole velocity are all 0.05
The constructor's continuous flag defaults to False, so the discrete action space is selected
The two encoder sensors are 'slider' on slider_to_cart and 'pole' on cart_to_pole, attached in that order
The EncoderSensor fieldnames are Q and V, so its measurement matrix has a position row then a velocity row
The observation flattens the EncoderSensor measurement matrix with reshape((-1,))
The observation space is a Box with the symmetric position bounds [X_THRESHOLD, THETA_THRESHOLD] and the robot's velocity limit
The three discrete commands are -command_limit, zero and +command_limit, where command_limit is the motor effort limit
The action space is Discrete(len(AVAIL_CTRL)) when continuous is False
The cart motor effort limit is 10 N
The cart is 1.0 kg
The pole is a 0.1 kg point mass at 1.0 m from its joint
The simulation uses the euler_explicit integrator with dtMax = CONTROL_DT
A reset samples cart position and pole angle, then cart velocity and pole velocity, from the environment's np_random generator
A discrete action selects its force from AVAIL_CTRL
The reward is 1.0 if the episode is not terminated and 0.0 otherwise
By default has_terminated returns terminated=False and truncates when the observation is out of bounds
A step truncates when the observation is out of bounds or the simulation exceeds simulation_duration_max
The default simulation_duration_max is 86400 s

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial state and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random while upstream derives its generator from numpy SeedSequence/SFC64, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: the fake is a point-mass cart-pole in pure Python, not the Jiminy engine: no contact, friction, actuator dynamics, sensor noise or rendering; it was never compared with a real gym_jiminy run
the fake seeds Python random.Random; upstream's BaseJiminyEnv._initialize_seed derives a numpy SeedSequence/SFC64 state (generic.py:383-388), so one seed gives different trajectories on the two
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (STEP_DT 0.02 s) only
the registration id 'cartpole' resolves through gymnasium.make only after gym_jiminy.envs has been imported to run its register() calls; that sim path was not run here
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: CartPoleJiminyEnv defines no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop neither step nor reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last state stays readable
